subject.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue

question: Should a durable wake become terminally `delivered` as soon as its event is durably enqueued into the owning session’s delivery queue, even though the session has not consumed it and no external delivery occurred?
rationale: The code can implement either ownership model, but choosing the durable wake’s terminal meaning, reset-generation behavior, and responsibility after queue retry exhaustion defines a persisted product contract that automation cannot infer safely.

options.title: Accept queue ownership transfer
options.body: Treat successful idempotent enqueue as durable delivery, retain explicit `session_delivery_queue` and `noExternalSend` evidence, and make later queue recovery solely responsible for consumption.

options.title: Wait for queue consumption
options.body: Keep the wake non-terminal until the queue reports successful session consumption, requiring a new cross-owner acknowledgment and failure-reconciliation contract.

options.title: Introduce a handed-off state
options.body: Add a distinct persisted state between pending and delivered so queue ownership transfer cannot be confused with consumption, at the cost of broader schema, protocol, and migration work.

recommendation.title: Accept queue ownership transfer
recommendation.body: Treat successful idempotent enqueue as durable delivery, retain explicit `session_delivery_queue` and `noExternalSend` evidence, and make later queue recovery solely responsible for consumption.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision directly extends the session-delivery ownership and recovery contract introduced in their merged queue work.
